subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add a new core sub-agent lifecycle contract with `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed`, or solve startup silence through the existing terminal outcome and diagnostic surfaces?
rationale: The source-level bug is credible, but the requested solution creates a new core lifecycle event surface that must be accepted across gateway, session, SDK, docs, and subagent consumers before automation can safely implement it.

options.title: Approve a fresh lifecycle contract
options.body: Request a current-main PR that wires `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` through embedded-agent, gateway wait/session, SDK normalization, docs, tests, and real startup-failure proof.

options.title: Use existing terminal semantics
options.body: Reject new phases for now and require a narrower repair that makes aborted startup visible through current terminal outcome and diagnostic paths.

options.title: Defer for live fixture proof
options.body: Wait for a shareable representative transcript or live reproduction before accepting new API semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve a fresh lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Request a current-main PR that wires `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` through embedded-agent, gateway wait/session, SDK normalization, docs, tests, and real startup-failure proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Historical lifecycle ownership and cross-surface product judgment make this the best available routing candidate from the observed history.
